fields.value: Mind(d)ing the President: A text analytic approach to measuring tax news

dsDescriptionValue.value:
This data set contains supplementary materials for "Mind(d)ing the President: A text analytic approach to measuring tax news".

It consists of the estimation results of the topic model and the estimated tax news measures.

Folder LDA contains data and code for replicating the topic modelling results and figures.

Folder TaxNews contains data and code for replicating the econometric analysis and figures.

value:
Text data (speeches) comes from the Public Papers of the Presidents - https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/

Tax liability changes and list of announcements - Romer,  C.  D.  and  D.  H.  Romer  (2009b).  Replication  data  for:   The  macroeconomic effects of tax changes:  Estimates based on a new measure of fiscal shocks. Nashville,  TN:  American  Economic  Association  [publisher],  2010.  Ann  Arbor, MI:  Inter-university  Consortium  for  Political  and  Social  Research  [distributor].https://doi.org/10.3886/E112357V1

Unanticipated tax liability changes - Mertens, K. and M. O. Ravn (2014). A reconciliation of SVAR and narrative estimatesof tax multipliers.Journal of Monetary Economics  68, S1–S19.

List of announcements and legislative lag dates - Yang, S.-C. S. (2007). A chronology of postwar US federal income tax policy. CAEPR Working  Papers  2007-021,  Center  for  Applied  Economics  and  Policy  Research, Indiana University.

Implicit tax rate - Leeper, E. M., A. W. Richter, and T. B. Walker (2012).  Quantitative effects of fiscal foresight. American Economic Journal:  Economic Policy  4(2), 115–44.

Macroeconomic data - U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis; U.S. Bureau of Labour Statistics; Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas; Federal Reserve Board; Robert Shiller (see Table C.1)

files.description:
List of speeches identified as tax announcements by Romer and Romer (2009) and Yang (2007).

The first 8 digits of 'Code' indicate the date of the speech (YYYYMMDD). The following 2 digits indicate the number of the speech within given day.

'Policy' is the name eventually given to the announced legislation.

'Direction' indicates whether the legislation resulted in net increase (1) or decrease (-1) of tax liabilities.

'Mixed' indicated whether the legislation consisted of both measures that increased and decreased certain taxes.

'Description' is the name given to the speech in the Public Papers of the Presidents.
files.label: tax_speeches.csv
